content.text: Why do some appliances cost more to run than others? Why does a kettle heat water faster than a phone charger? The answer lies in electrical power—the rate at which electrical energy is transferred. Understanding power helps us compare appliances, calculate running costs, and choose appropriate fuses.
Electrical power is the rate of energy transfer, measured in watts (W). The key formulae are P = IV, P = I²R, and P = V²/R.

A typical kettle uses about 2-3 kW, while a phone charger uses only about 5 W. The kettle transfers energy 400-600 times faster, which is why it heats water so quickly.
— Power is rate of energy use. A 1 kW appliance used for 1 hour uses 1 kWh of energy.
